rule: A ruling is superseded when a later CBP ruling in the corpus states that it is revoked or modified: the EFFECT ON OTHER RULINGS section, any "is/are hereby revoked/modified" or "we hereby revoke/modify" sentence, a subject line that starts "Revocation of" or "Modification of/to", or a later ruling stating that one ruling "was revoked/modified by" another. The date is the superseding ruling's issue date. Notices of proposed revocation and affirmations are not supersessions. A ruling revoked after a case date stays usable for that case. Final revocations and modifications published in fetched Customs Bulletin notices are added, dated by the notice's effective date, with the bulletin's volume, number, page and URL (D400); proposed ones are listed under "proposed" and never bar a precedent.
